title: Nachaquatuck (Cold Spring Harbor Creek)
summary: Nachaquatuck names the creek or river at Cold Spring Harbor that marked Huntington's western boundary, linking the placename to boundary language and tidal-stream geography.
map_geometry_source: approximate head of Cold Spring Harbor / Huntington-Oyster Bay boundary marker; not an exact deed survey point
history_content: Cold Spring Harbor creek, Huntington boundary context, and ending tidal stream interpretation are brought together here. Time-specific documentary context is handled as a Historic Moment.
translation_content:
Alternate forms include Nachaquetack, Naccaquetack, Nackaquatok, Nackaquatack, and Nachquatuck. The meaning is given as the ending tidal stream, from a phrase meaning at the end of joined to a tidal-stream element.

Why Place Names Matter

“Most place-names will through their meaning reveal something about the individual locality, but only if the name has been interpreted correctly.”

— Names in Denmark, University of Copenhagen, Place-Names (n.d.), How is a name formed? section
whereintheworld_content: The point is an approximate general marker near the head of Cold Spring Harbor and the Huntington/Oyster Bay boundary area. It is not an exact deed-boundary survey point.
